baseline_commit_message: Tranche W — activation, hot-path demolition, and three distinct cliffs
description: Benchmark baseline captured after Tranche W. The tranche is the audit-driven response to the V.11 'spent without gain' state: csp_recognizers.rs had zero csp_solver:: references, backend/kernels/ had zero production consumers, CostWeights was shared by type only, the strategy solvers ran priority cascades that ignored ir.recognizer_decisions, and OptimizationMode::MinimizeCost was invoked zero times anywhere in the workspace. Tranche W activates the V.4/V.6 substrate, demolishes the three distinct compile-time cliffs identified by profiling (factor_literal_prefixes, grammar-tier e-graph lifecycle, HIR-tier per-pattern saturation), eliminates the seven hot-path clones the audit flagged, and lands the parser-side wins from the cargo-expand audit (POD enum Copy + alloc_slice_copy, hoisted digit/alnum scanners). The legacy csp_recognizers.rs is deleted; csp_strategy.rs replaces it with a real csp_solver::Csp running OptimizationMode::MinimizeCost. backend/kernels/ has six of eight family modules wired through scanner_plan.rs and emit_delim_scan_impl as production consumers; the remaining two (prefix_class, sep_list) are documented for the V.7→V.8 transposition follow-up.
arch: four-layer optimizer: e-graph (equivalence) / facts (legality) / CSP (choice) / backend (emission). Tranche W activates the substrate built in V.1-V.10. CostConfig threads through every consumer (egraph::CostConfig + bbnf_ir::CostConfig wrapper); GrammarCostModel and RegexExtractionCost both read from it. The grammar-tier e-graph and HIR-tier e-graph both pre-size their hash-cons tables from the source node count via EGraph::with_capacity. The strategy CSP (csp_strategy.rs) builds one Csp per rule body with StrategyDomain (cost-aware FiniteDomain), adds ImplicationConstraint for parent-child compatibility, and solves via solve_optimized() with MinimizeCost. A no-cross-constraint fast path elides finalize+solve when no implication constraints fire, picking the per-variable minimum directly. backend/strategy/alt_strategy.rs is now a thin lookup against ir.recognizer_decisions with the AllLiteral structural fast-path preserved (it depends on the backend ValuePlacement::Inline context that the IR pipeline doesn't model). backend/kernels/{quoted_string, number, comment_ws, identifier, balanced_wrap, charclass} are real production callers; the regex emit registry routes through them.

notes.compile_time_demolition: All compile-pipeline rows improved substantially. The CSS L4 cliff (factor_literal_prefixes rebuilding the dedup map per recursive call, ~92% inclusive on the post-V profile) is gone — phase 0's FactorCtx lift dropped compile_css_l4 from 98 ms to 9.2 ms (-90.6%). The compile_bbnf cliff (drop_in_place<EGraph<GrammarENode>> + rayon LockLatch::wait_and_reset, ~50% combined on post-V) was attacked from both sides: phase 1 added EGraph::with_capacity hash-cons sizing and bumped the rayon parallelism threshold from 16 to a per-CostConfig 128. Most other benches benefit from the threshold bump alone (compile_css_mono -56%, compile_sheets -48.6%, compile_ebnf -16.2%).
notes.compile_json_gate: compile_json finished at -4.8% versus the plan's -10% gate. The grammar is small (4 rules, 4 regex patterns) — it's dominated by fixed pipeline overhead (lowering, type projection, dispatch tables) that the tranche doesn't touch. Phase 2's HIR e-graph trivial-skip helped, but the 5 µs gap to the gate is dominated by per-rule strategy CSP construction that the existing fast-path doesn't fully elide on small grammars. The gap is acknowledged; closing it requires a global (cross-rule) CSP allocation strategy that's in the V.7 → V.8 follow-up tranche scope.
notes.parse_time_wins: All CSS L4 parse benches improved by 11-15% — the compounded effect of phase 5b (parser enum derives Copy, BumpSlab uses alloc_slice_copy memcpy fast path), phase 5d (kernels::charclass routes [0-9]+ / [a-zA-Z0-9]+ / [0-9a-fA-F]+ to scan_digits_mut / scan_alnum_mut / scan_hex_mut), phase 3d (every shared scanner now goes through a backend::kernels family module). JSON parses see smaller wins (1-7%) — the JSON grammar already had its dispatch and slab paths optimized in earlier tranches.
notes.csp_solver_activation: Tranche W is the first production use of csp_solver::Csp::solve_optimized(MinimizeCost) in the bbnf workspace. Per the architectural commitment in plan §3 rule 3, this satisfies 'OptimizationMode::MinimizeCost is invoked at least once in production code'. The strategy CSP runs per-rule with cost-weighted StrategyDomain<StrategyValue> variables and ImplicationConstraint cross-variable constraints. A no-constraint fast path picks the per-variable minimum directly without finalize+solve when no constraint fires.
notes.kernels_consumer_count: 6 of 8 backend/kernels/ family modules now have at least one real production caller (per plan §5 hard gate 'backend/kernels/ consumer count ≥ 1 production caller per family module'): quoted_string, number, comment_ws, identifier, balanced_wrap, charclass. The remaining two (prefix_class, sep_list) are deferred to the V.7→V.8 transposition follow-up — both touch the sep-by emission path which is more invasive than tranche W's gestalt scope.
notes.follow_up_blockers: The legacy backend/patterns/{delim_scan,key_dispatch,cache,mod}.rs deletion that plan §8 calls for is deferred. The detection halves are still consumed by alt_strategy.rs's structural fallback (when ir.recognizer_decisions doesn't cover an Alt) and by the dispatch.rs delim-scan caller. Removing them requires migrating the structural detection upstream into the recognizer mining pass + the strategy CSP's domain feasibility phase, which is the V.7 → V.8 transposition follow-up. The csp_recognizers.rs deletion DID land in W.3b — it's the file that the plan's gate '0 csp_recognizers references' covers.
